clue.text: Nearly sick swallowing a brown and black

indicators.note: swallowing says the shortened word takes the next pieces inside it
nearly means the word for ill is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: sick here is the word itself, whose first three letters go on
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: Someone feeling queasy after gulping down a brown and black drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brown and black' reads like a colour pairing; 'black' alone is the definition, in its sense of wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic deeds are evil, and black is a common figurative word for wicked or devilish.

clue.text: Embarrassed with cigarette remains in a bed

indicators.note: in says the cigarette leavings are placed inside a bed

parts.note: taken as written
ash is what is left of a smoked cigarette

explanation.surface: A mortified smoker finds ash in the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abashed is to be made ashamed or embarrassed, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Cut festival flower

indicators.note: cut tells us to chop a letter off the front of the festival's name

parts.note: Easter is the Christian spring festival

explanation.surface: A trimmed bloom for a holiday display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' removes the first letter of EASTER, leaving ASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The aster is a daisy-like garden plant, so it is an example of a flower.

clue.text: Glib one could be vile

indicators.note: could be suggests these letters might be rearranged into something else

parts.note: the anagram fodder, seven letters

explanation.surface: A smooth talker might turn out to be a nasty piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges GLIBONE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble means base or dishonourable, close in sense to vile.

clue.text: Prime minister once had to resign in the wood

indicators.note: in says the word for resigning sits inside the tree name

parts.note: ash is a tree and its timber
quit is to resign, here in its past form

explanation.surface: A former premier stepped down while out in the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: H. H. Asquith was British Prime Minister from 1908 to 1916; 'the wood' is a tree name, not a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Asquith led the British government before and during the early First World War, a past premier.

clue.text: Makes love in silence but then makes a noise

indicators.note: in says the courting verb is placed within the call for quiet

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
woos means courts, makes love in the old sense

explanation.surface: A couple courting quietly then breaks the hush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes love' is the old sense of courting, not sex.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoosh is to move with a rushing sound, so it means to make that kind of noise.

clue.text: Relaxing from the world's roundabout

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, stands for the world's nations together
winding means circuitous, roundabout

explanation.surface: Taking it easy, away from the world's spinning merry-go-round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roundabout' looks like the British traffic circle or fairground ride; here it is an adjective meaning indirect.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwinding is an idiom for relaxing after tension, as a coiled spring lets go.

clue.text: Sprucest bird fades away within

indicators.note: within says the dying verb sits inside the small bird

parts.note: the tit is a small songbird
dies away means fades

explanation.surface: The neatest bird slowly withers in its cage.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce means neat and trim, so the sprucest is the neatest or most orderly.

clue.text: Small quality potato skins for violent prisoners

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic or quality
a jacket potato is baked in its skin, so jackets are potato skins

explanation.surface: A menu of little potato skins served to inmates.
explanation.walkthrough: A jacket potato is the British baked potato in its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Straitjackets are restraining garments put on prisoners or patients who are violent, a definition by purpose.

clue.text: All characters die

definitions.meaning: a play's ... is its full set of characters or actors
a mould, which is what a die is

explanation.definitionFit: The cast is every performer in a show, and a cast or die is a mould for shaping metal.

clue.text: General gets people off the mark

parts.note: a nation is a people
wide means missing the target, off the mark

explanation.surface: A commanding officer gets troops going from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army officer but is the adjective; 'off the mark' looks like starting, but means inaccurate. 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationwide means extending across the whole nation, so it is general or widespread.

clue.text: Offspring holds on to her angel

indicators.note: holds on to says the young animal clasps the pronoun inside it

parts.note: a cub is the young of a lion or bear
taken as written

explanation.surface: A child clings to its mother, sweet as an angel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a type of angel, often painted as a winged child.

clue.text: Non-worker directed in a quiz

indicators.note: in says the dispatched word goes inside the contest name

parts.note: a bee is a competition, as in spelling bee
sent means directed or dispatched

explanation.surface: Someone skipping work is sent off to a trivia contest.
explanation.walkthrough: A bee is a gathering for a contest, as in a spelling bee, which is why it can stand for a quiz.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is someone missing from where they should be, such as a worker who fails to turn up.

clue.text: Followers head off to get payments

indicators.note: off means out of order, so the letters of head are jumbled

parts.note: rents are regular payments for property

explanation.surface: Disciples lop off their leader's head to collect the dues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' looks like a beheading instruction; 'off' is the anagram signal on 'head'. 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherents are supporters or devotees, people who follow a cause or leader.

clue.text: Seriously, it's too soon to build a home for the young inside

indicators.note: inside says the nursery word sits within the word for premature

parts.note: early means before the proper time
a nest is where birds raise their young

explanation.surface: A gravely spoken warning that it is premature to build a nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to build a' is linking, and 'home for the young' looks like a nursery or orphanage before it settles on a bird's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnestly means with sincere and serious intent, so it is a synonym of seriously.

clue.text: Blue stain

definitions.meaning: to stain is to soil or make filthy

explanation.definitionFit: A blue joke is smutty and indecent, and to soil or mark something with a stain is to make it grubby.

clue.text: It's boring round Iowa, according to this book

indicators.note: round says the dull word goes around the state code

parts.note: dry means dull and boring
IA is the postal code for the US state of Iowa

explanation.surface: A journal claims that life around Iowa is tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'according to this' is linking, so the definition is just 'book'.
explanation.definitionFit: A diary is a book in which daily events are recorded.

clue.text: Set up made from bent tins completely

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: all means wholly, completely

explanation.surface: A structure made entirely from crumpled cans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To install something is to set it up in position ready for use.

clue.text: Dawn's innards?

parts.note: the first light of morning is a word whose plural also names one's vital organs, as in beating the living lights out of someone

explanation.walkthrough: Daylight comes at dawn, and 'the living daylights' in British idiom means one's insides, as in scaring them out of you.
explanation.definitionFit: Daylights is an informal word for a person's vital organs or wits, and daylight is what dawn brings.

clue.text: Old music hall star keeping end of turn clean

indicators.note: keeping says the performer holds the final letter inside

parts.note: Sir Harry Lauder was a Scottish music hall entertainer

indicators.note: end of says only the last letter of the word turn is used

explanation.surface: A veteran variety performer keeps his act wholesome.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Lauder was a Scottish star of British music hall, the old variety theatre; a turn is a music hall act.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder is to wash clothes, or figuratively to make dirty money look clean.

clue.text: Sailor captures victims

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
gets means seizes or captures

explanation.surface: A seaman seizes the people he preys on.
explanation.definitionFit: Targets are those aimed at or singled out for attack, so they are victims.

clue.text: Cutlery for this side of beef

definitions.meaning: silverware is cutlery made of precious metal
silverside is a cut of beef, so this word goes before side

explanation.walkthrough: SILVERSIDE is a British cut of beef from the hindquarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver is household cutlery, and with side added it names a cut of beef.

clue.text: Mark tries unexpectedly to stretch demand

indicators.note: to stretch means the asking word is pulled wide to fit something inside

parts.note: ask means request or demand

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters of tries are turned about

explanation.surface: A teacher's mark makes unexpected attempts at stretching a request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' gives TERIS from 'tries', which 'to stretch' places inside the requesting word.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is a star-shaped mark used in printing.

clue.text: Moderate anger following pump that won't start

indicators.note: following says the angry word comes after the shortened pump
that won't start says the first letter of pump is removed

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: Calming an angry outburst after a pump fails to start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' is a verb here, as in refereeing, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To umpire is to referee or arbitrate a dispute, so to moderate it.

clue.text: Lever's part of a bell-shaped alarm

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lever forms part of a bell-shaped alarm clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'bell-shaped': belL-SHAPED gives PED and alarm adds AL; the 's of 'Lever's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedal is a foot-operated lever, as on a bicycle or piano.

clue.text: Fixed cat — vet paid and delighted

indicators.note: fixed here hints at arranging things anew, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: part of the anagram fodder
part of the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: The neutered cat's owner was thrilled to pay the vet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixed' is a euphemism for neutering a pet, but here signals rearranging CAT and VETPAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Captivated means charmed and enchanted, close in sense to delighted.

clue.text: You can read this document whichever way you like

indicators.note: whichever way you like says the word reads the same from either end

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A legal paper that can be read in any direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You can read this' is a link to 'whichever way you like', which says the answer is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is a legal document, such as one transferring ownership of property.

clue.text: Contestants' parking needs rows

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs
layers are tiers, rows set one above another

explanation.surface: Competitors' car park needs to be laid out in rows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is a link; P + LAYERS gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Players are those taking part in a game, so contestants.

clue.text: Natural but becomes brutal when he joins

indicators.note: joins is read in reverse here: the answer is what is left of the cruel word before the pronoun is attached

parts.note: heartless means cruel or brutal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A simple, unaffected person turns cruel once a man joins in.
explanation.walkthrough: Add HE to the answer and it becomes HEARTLESS (brutal); so the answer is HEARTLESS without HE. 'becomes' and 'when' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless means without guile or artifice, so natural and unaffected.
